newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel approves oil deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel approves oil deregulation bill.

text.p: A bill regulating the opening of Brazil's petroleum industry to private competition was approved in a Senate panel and was set to advance to other committees in the upper house, a congressional official said on Wednesday.
The 23-member Constitution and Justice Committee voted through a show of hands in favor of the bill, with only two members registering their opposition, the official said.

The bill must now be heard by the Economic Affairs and Infrastructure committees. The government might seek to fuse those hearings to speed up passage of the bill through the Senate, the official said.

The legislation sets out details of a constitutional amendment, approved in Congress in 1995, that allowed private natural gas and oil companies to compete against Petrobras or go into partnership with the state-owned monopoly.
The bill, approved in March by the Chamber of Deputies, would also set up a regulator to oversee the industry.

Petrobras is considering more than 100 proposed joint ventures involving private companies. The projects would more than double Brazil's oil output of about 860,000 barrels a day. (( -- William Schomberg, Brasilia newsroom 5561 2230358))
